positive_text:
We had a really great stay and would definitely recommend this hotel!

The room was very clean, well organised and comfortable, and everything was exactly as we expected. The Wi-Fi worked perfectly throughout our stay, and the access system with the entry code was very simple, convenient and made everything feel easy and secure.

A special thank you to Alona and Julie, who were absolutely amazing and so friendly! Even though the reception process was virtual when we arrived, they assisted us through the computer with the check-in and made the whole experience incredibly smooth. Everything was explained clearly, communication was excellent, and the process was quick and straightforward with no unnecessary complications or bureaucracy. We really appreciated how helpful, patient and welcoming they were.

The location is also very convenient. It’s easy to get around using public transport, and being close to Allianz stadium and Bondi Beach is definitely a big plus, especially if you want to explore one of Sydney’s most popular areas.

Overall, we really enjoyed the practicality of the hotel, the cleanliness, the location and especially the excellent customer service. Everything worked perfectly from check-in to check-out.

Thank you again to Alona and Julie for making our stay even better. We would happily stay here again!

Horrible experience checking in with Reyna and Sophia.

I messaged them at 11:00 in the morning to let them know that I wanted dinner. I also completed the online check-in, uploaded all my details, and was told I would receive a door code.

I arrived at the hotel at 7:00 pm and immediately emailed them and sent messages through Booking.com. Reyna ignored these messages until 7:42 pm.

When I finally spoke to her, I was given a series of different and contradictory explanations. First, I was told that none of my emails or Booking.com messages had been received. When I showed her evidence that they had been sent, the explanations changed.

I was then kept waiting for another 15 minutes while further explanations were given. I finally got through the door at around 8:00 pm.

I went to get the dinner I had requested earlier, only to find that there was no dinner available. I went back to reception to speak to Reyna, and again I was given a series of explanations that contradicted what I had previously been told.

I was left standing at reception with all my bags until approximately 8:20 pm. Reyna then gave me the wrong door code and refused to provide the contact details for her manager or supervisor.

By contrast, the gentleman who is normally on the screen on a Friday night has always been excellent and provides a completely different level of customer service.

My impression was that Reyna was worried about her handling of the situation being exposed, which is why I felt I was given different explanations, my questions weren't properly answered, and I was refused the manager's email address.

This was an absolutely horrible experience. The whole situation was unnecessarily stressful and time-consuming. Reyna's handling of the situation was extremely poor.

As we do not reserve or hold individual portions, we’re unable to guarantee a meal for guests who arrive after the dinner service has ended. This is in place to help us manage food safely and fairly for all guests.

That said, we acknowledge that this should have been communicated clearly to you in advance, particularly after you had contacted us about dinner. We apologise for any misunderstanding or inconvenience this caused.

Regarding the check-in and door-code issues, we understand how frustrating it must have been to wait with your luggage and receive an incorrect code. We are reviewing the circumstances and communication with the team involved to ensure that guests receive clear and accurate information and prompt assistance when issues arise.

We appreciate your feedback and are sorry that your arrival did not reflect the level of service we aim to provide.

I had stayed at this property several times last year, and while the customer service wasn’t always outstanding, I understood it’s a hostel environment. However, during one stay, I was placed right next to a bathroom, and there was constant door slamming throughout the night (2–4am). Understandably, I was frustrated and contacted reception via the intercom. Unfortunately, I was told there were no options to move rooms and that I would just have to put up with it.
The following morning, the manager informed me that I was no longer welcome, despite having stayed there for nearly two months the previous year and across multiple locations. I found this response extreme and unjustified. When I tried to discuss the situation, the manager was combative, dismissive, and ultimately hung up on me, stating he didn’t care and that I was effectively evicted.
I also later received a note about a bottle of rosé wine, even though I was not drinking and have never done so on the premises, which added to the confusion.
I want to highlight that Lia, a staff member, consistently provided excellent customer service—professional, helpful, and respectful at all times.
Months later, when I returned to Sydney, I even apologized in an attempt to stay again, though I’m not sure why I felt the need to. My reservation was declined regardless.
Overall, the situation felt disproportionate and poorly handled. I was left confused, as the outcome didn’t seem to match the circumstances.

title: Not as advertised and poorly maintained.
negative_text:
Unfortunately, this hostel does not match the photos or description shown on Booking. The exterior and interior look significantly different from what is advertised, and the overall condition of the property is far below expectations.
There is also inconsistent information provided to guests. The document sent at check-in states that check-in is at 2:00pm, yet staff strictly enforce a 3:00pm check-in and explained that the document is “outdated.” If policies have changed, official documents provided to guests should be updated accordingly to avoid confusion.
Check-in is restricted due to “cleaning,” however, upon arrival, the room was clearly not properly cleaned. Floors were not vacuumed, trash was left behind, and during my three-night stay, the room was never cleaned. The document also states that bed sheets are changed daily unless requested otherwise and that rooms are cleaned every day. Neither of these services were provided.
On my last day, after previous guests checked out, I pointed out leftover trash to the cleaning staff. When I returned later that evening, the trash was still there. The only action taken was placing a new garbage bag.
There is only one bathroom per floor for approximately four or five rooms, resulting in constant queues. The bathroom was noisy, poorly maintained, and lacked basic amenities. Towels are not provided and cost $10 to rent, which is significantly higher than typical hostel rates.
Breakfast and dinner are advertised as included, but both are offered only within a very limited one-hour window, which is impractical given the number of guests. Dinner was extremely basic, with no beverages included. When water was requested, only tap water was offered. Considering the overall hygiene standards of the property, this was concerning.
There is no physical reception — communication is via a remote screen, and assistance was limited and inconsistent.

title: Que sea barato no implica que su mantenimiento sea deficiente.
positive_text:
Si estás valorando este hostel en tu estancia en Sydney posiblemente será por su ubicación y porque es de los que incluye desayuno y cena en el precio.

Posiblemente ambos puntos son sus claras ventajas para decidirse frente a otros, aunque con matices.

Respecto a la ubicación, personalmente creo que es su punto fuerte. Bien conectado a la estación central de tren, está en un punto que andando puedes llegar a Circular Quay en apenas 30-40 minutos andando a un ritmo normal. Estás en un punto que si te decides por ir a The Rocks, o a la zona de Chinatown, también está a menos de 30 minutos andando, por lo que estás prácticamente en el centro de todo.
Si además planeas acercarte a Bondi Beach desde aquí, hay línea de autobús y en menos de 1h de trayecto estás allí con un solo transbordo.

Otro de sus puntos positivos, en mi caso debo destacar las habitaciones. Literas rígidas y cómodas que no se mueven en absoluto (si has ido a otros hostel sabes de lo que hablo). Colchones decentes por el precio a pagar y habitación relativamente correcta en cuanto a espacio (al menos en las habitaciones de 6 personas).

Por último, la parte del desayuno y cena que incluyen en el precio. Desde luego que es una ventaja frente a otras opciones de hostel que no incluyen nada. Desayuno básico que se sirve de 7:30am a 9am, incluye zumo, leche, té/café, cereales y pan de molde con diferentes mermeladas, mantequilla y crema de cacahuete. Eso es todo. Simple y básico. Y lo mismo ocurre en la cena. Horario de 18:30pm a 19:45pm, suelen ser platos básicos donde no podemos destacar que sean las mejores opciones nutritivamente hablando. Pasta algunos días, pollo con puré de patata otros, o arroz con carne picada. No esperes la mejor cena posible, de hecho da más sensación de comedor social que de hostel.
negative_text:
Soy crítico porque en mis últimos 5 meses viajando he estado en muchos hostel y entiendo que si busco las opciones más económicas, renuncio a ciertas comodidades que otros más caros si me ofrecen (como más cantidad de baños, cocinas más grandes y más equipadas, zonas comunes de mejor calidad y más amplias, etc).

Lo que no está bien es la falta de mantenimiento general del lugar. Es un hostel viejo si nos centramos en sus comodidades, y salvo las habitaciones que a mi parecer estaban en buen estado general, el resto fue bastante decepcionante.

La mayoría de baños estaban viejos y no funcionaban como deberían. Ya sea un grifo roto, una ducha sin mucha presión de agua u otro con el suelo siempre con agua. Se notaba una falta de mantenimiento del lugar. Por no decir que en general estaban sucios. Paredes de las duchas por ejemplo que dudo se hayan limpiado en los últimos meses, papeleras llenas muchas ocasiones, y en definitiva, sensación de abandono.

Por supuesto, entiendo que pagar un precio reducido por una noche en Sydney con desayuno y cena incluido, tienes que renunciar a cierto confort en tu estancia. Pero eso no implica llegar a un lugar con poco mantenimiento y con zonas sucias en general.

Bereits beim Betreten des Eingangs fiel ein sehr unangenehmer Geruch auf, der stark an einen nassen Hund erinnerte. Speiseraum war ungepflegt und überhaupt nicht einladend, um dort seine Mahlzeiten einzunehmen. Tische und Wände waren sichtbar dreckig.

Die Toiletten erinnerten eher an öffentliche WCs am Hauptbahnhof – so unappetitlich, dass man sich regelrecht davor ekelte, dort zu duschen. Auch die Vorhänge und Betten waren befleckt und schmutzig.

Nach Rücksprache mit dem Hostelpersonal wurde uns mitgeteilt, dass Reinigungsmittel zur Verfügung stehen. Ganz ehrlich: Es ist zwar ein Hostel und man erwartet keinen Luxus, aber zu verlangen, dass Gäste selbst den Dreck anderer beseitigen, weil das Housekeeping nicht hinterherkommt, ist schlichtweg frech.

Alles in allem kann ich nur sagen: Verlasst euch nicht auf die positiven Bewertungen dieses Hostels – sie spiegeln die Realität absolut nicht wider.

title: Great experience at Azzurro
positive_text:
I loved staying at Azzurro. The location is one of the best in the whole city, it has a beautiful view of the Opera House and it's close to a lot of useful establishments for students and backpackers, such as the Kings Cross library, the Kings Cross train station, supermarkets, grocery stores, washing house, pubs, restaurants and more.

The hostel fulfills the proposal of being a non party hostel. Despite that, this is the perfect place to be surrounded by people from several countries and it's very easy to make friends, people are very kind and friendly.

The beds are very comfortable, mostly because of the bedding set and the curtains they have in it.

The staff is great, they are friendly and whatever you need they will help.
negative_text:
The common areas are not very clean, especially the tables, and there's not much space to put your supermarket things in the storerooms or in the fridges, so try not to buy a lot of things!!!

The hostel is not responsible for your belongings, so keep a careful eye to your belongings, mostly small things, for example, jewelery or your umbrella, because people will steal it. I'm not saying this is a characteristic of this hostel. It could happen anywhere, but be careful.

The food could be better and have more meal variations, but, at least, they are very generous about it, so it's impossible to starve.

title: I went to the room and left
positive_text: I don't have any positive feedback. I found the info on the page confusing and the experience frustrating
negative_text: I turned up to the room and I thought I had booked a room with 2 bunk beds and a private bathroom. It said twin so I thought I had booked for the 2 people even though I was traveling on my own. I wanted to book the room for myself and was happy to pay for both. The price looked to be double the single person rate. But someone else, a stranger, was already sleeping in the bottom bunk when I arrived. I have back issues so the top bunk was not very easy for me and I had thought I would be able to use the bottom bunk when I made the booking. I recently did a similar thing at another place in Bondi. It was only 9pm and the other person already had their stuff literally all over the place, in the room, the kitchenette and the bathroom, and they were already asleep in the bottom bunk. They also had the aircon blaring on some hot setting so the room was like an oven. I tried to message the chat as there was no staff there that I could find and they took ages to reply. I asked if there was another room I could change to and they said no they were already booked. I asked for a locker I could use to put my personal things in with a lock. They finally replied and said there was a locker but you have to bring your own lock. Which I didn't have with me... and I did not see info about this on the pages or messages/emails. It was very heavy rain outside so I sat in the kitchen for a bit to try and figure out what to do.. I decided to book a room at another hotel near by which was expensive but I needed to be able to sleep for the next day of work and not have to sleep in some kind of sauna with a stranger and no security for my belongings. I don't usually leave negative reviews but I was really put out with this experience. They did try to apologise on the chat and offer me a different private room for another night with a small discount but I was only staying one night in Sydney for work. Much clearer info on the page would have helped.

7) The aircon was in the room set to 23 degrees, I asked staff at around 9pm and they said there should be a remote in the room, there wasn’t so they said they’ll send someone. They 2 hours later (around 11pm) and I asked them to switch airon off he refused saying it would get too hot. It was Autumn. He said to call if too cold, so I did they said someone will come. They came just before 1AM to switch it off. I was sleeping.
8) I did not want to stay another night so I left in the morning and was refused a refund for the night I wasn’t staying. I gave numerous opportunities to resolve this but I think it’s important to leave an honest review. I’ve stayed in many hostels internationally and I will take bad reviews with a pinch of salt if photos and rating seems good, but I think this is the worst I’ve stayed in. The photos are very misleading, it looks nice on the photos but the reality is far from it. The vibe in terms of décor, smell, cleanliness and even other people there is SO depressing. I was so much happier when I went to a YHA instead.
9) Bathrooms are small, so get soaked and gross and not enough of them.

negative_text:

Maybe they should advise people to use public transportation on the first day or have a better map of the area with clear instructions on how to navigate those bridges if you are trying to walk to the place coming from the Central Station. negative_text:
Nous avons séjourné dans une chambre double privée pendant plusieurs nuits et avons été très déçus.

🔒 Sécurité : De la nourriture a été volée directement dans notre chambre pendant notre absence. Il n’y a que le personnel de ménage qui avait le code de la porte. Aucune solution ni compensation proposée. C’est inadmissible.

Repas inclus : Nous avons mangé la même chose tous les soirs pendant 6 jours : pâtes à la tomate et riz au curry avec un peu de poulet. Pour le prix, on aurait pu faire nos courses, manger plus varié et pour moins cher.

Confort de la chambre : Pas de vraies fenêtres fermées, seulement des dalles pivotantes en verre, donc bruit constant. Le store restait fermé car la fenêtre donnait directement sur un passage. Il y avait aussi un trou pour la ventilation, ce qui n’aide pas au calme.

Nuisances sonores : L’insonorisation est inexistante. On entend tout : les gens dans les escaliers extérieurs (Butlers Stairs), les discussions, les joints fumés juste en bas de la fenêtre, comme s’ils étaient dans la chambre. Impossible de dormir sans bouchons d’oreilles.

Cuisine commune : Une seule plaque, pas assez de vaisselle (manque de mugs notamment), et peu de respect des règles (vaisselle sale non rangée, etc.). Et on y était en basse saison.

En résumé : Le rapport qualité-prix est très mauvais. Pour le même prix (voire moins cher), on aurait eu bien mieux dans un petit appartement avec cuisine. Nous ne recommandons pas du tout cet établissement.

title: Budget option for warmer days
positive_text:
The included breakfast and optional dinner are definitely highlights – breakfast is simple but sufficient, and the pre-order dinner is a convenient way to ensure a proper meal. The dinner I had was actually very good, and it’s a great benefit to have this option directly at the hostel.

The location is a plus – like most hostels around King’s Cross, there’s a terrace with a nice view of the Harbour Bridge.
That said, the overall experience might be more pleasant in warmer seasons.
negative_text:
However, one evening I asked for seconds, and the main cook told us to come back in 20 minutes. I waited over 30 minutes, and each time I approached, he just said “wait, wait” and served others instead. Eventually, there was nothing left, and I had to go out and buy food elsewhere – which felt like a big minus.

The room I stayed in was in the basement, quite cold and not very well insulated. I can’t imagine staying there during winter. The room was spacious, but everything creaked, and there was no power outlet for the upper bunk.
Also, the place felt dimly lit, which made it hard to find at first. The hostel operates in two separate buildings, but it’s not clear where you’re staying. After booking on Booking.com, you still need to register on the hostel’s website and then check in again at reception – which is unnecessarily complicated.

There is no larger lounge area in the accommodation where you can work or relax. Only an extended version of the dining room, which was always dirty, at least during my stay.

Overall, a fair option for travelers on a budget – especially during warmer days – but be prepared for some practical discomforts.

title: Unhygienic
positive_text:
This bathroom is an absolute disgrace. It looks like it hasn’t seen a proper clean or maintenance check in years. The tiles are stained and moldy, the floor is constantly wet and filthy, and the overall hygiene is frankly unacceptable. The shower area is particularly grim. There’s mold in the corners, grime in the grout, and a general stench of neglect.

The most ridiculous part? The “window.” There is no window. Just a wide open hole in the wall with rusted bars and a pathetic sign that says “Do not close the window.” Close what, exactly? The glass is completely gone. It is just an open gap to a dirty wall outside, with zero privacy and zero protection.

To make matters worse, I checked out four days early and received no compensation, refund, or even acknowledgment. I left the property well before my original check-out date, and despite following all proper procedures, no one offered any kind of reimbursement or explanation.

This isn’t just run-down. It shows a complete lack of care. It is one of those places you walk into and instantly regret. Avoid it if you have any choice.

I stayed at Potts Point for just one night as part of a longer business trip across Australia, and I was genuinely impressed by how comfortable and convenient the experience was.

The location is truly ideal—quiet and charming, yet still close to the action. It's just a short walk to the Town Hall station, which made getting around the city incredibly easy. I even managed to squeeze in a quick visit to Bondi Beach, which was only a few rides away—perfect for unwinding after a full day of meetings.

The hostel itself is well-designed and thoughtfully maintained. The backyard and dining area stood out to me as peaceful spots where you could relax, grab a cup of coffee, or get some work done if needed. It was clear that the staff take pride in keeping the place clean and organized—my private room was spotless, and the shared areas were tidy and welcoming.

Special mention goes to the receptionist, who was not only polite and professional but also very efficient. After a long day of travel and work, I appreciated how quick and smooth the check-in process was. They also gave great recommendations for nearby places to eat and how to get around easily.

All in all, Potts Point Hostel exceeded my expectations, especially for a short business stop. It’s a great blend of comfort, cleanliness, and location, with a touch of character that makes you feel more at home than in a typical hotel.

title: Crackden vibes
positive_text:
Location was really good and we enjoyed the inclusion of food but these were the only good things about this property.

Vastly different from the photos, it felt like staying in a crackden, our twin room was outside in what reminded me of a prison room. The front door was left open at all times during the day which meant anyone could’ve walked in or out and with no staff actually on site (you can see someone on an iPad near the door) if someone had walked in that shouldn’t be there, there was literally no one to stop them.

The kitchen/dining areas were consistently gross and I’m glad breakfast and dinner were provided as I wouldn’t want to cook in them. The food for breakfast and dinner was good, although you have to book for dinner. On our first night we booked via the link given to us after I did our online check in however we weren’t on the list. The staff member serving food was really rude to us but I argued it and showed them the booking and we ended up being given tiny portions. On another day I saw them turn a girl away who had probably done the same thing!

The outside chill out area is actually nice and has a good view of the harbour and the opera house. The location was really good, Potts Point itself is lovely and the walk from the hostel through the botanic gardens towards the main area was great.

The place overall has a very unfriendly vibe, there’s signs everywhere saying there’s cameras and if they see people stealing they will call the police. This was no joke as in one tiny dining room there were 6 cameras!! There’s also signs everywhere saying no talking/phone calling in the rooms. I understand completely about being respectful but this was extreme as it said anyone reported to be talking in the rooms would be ejected.

Overall it did our budget some good but I wouldn’t stay again. In our 7 months of (worldwide) travelling probably our least favourite place!
Has a great backyard, and the patio is ideal for relaxing, especially with the beautiful view of the Harbour Bridge. The Potts Point area is full of charming cafés, which I loved exploring1

From the start, it was inconvenient—I had to carry my suitcase up two flights of stairs. The rooms were very warm at night, and cleanliness was lacking. I stayed in a room with a shared bathroom for nearly a week, and it didn’t seem to be cleaned at all during that time. Basic amenities like body soap and shampoo weren’t provided, so after a long flight, I had to use hand soap to shower. There were also no hair dryers available.

There’s no staff on-site, so if you have any issues, you need to message them and wait for a response. The walls are quite thin, so noise carries easily. If guests are talking late at night or moving luggage around—which happened often—you’ll hear it, even with earplugs.

Unlike many hostels that offer USB ports at each bunk for convenience, this one doesn’t, so be sure to bring a converter.

I originally booked this place to save a little money because the photos looked promising, but unfortunately, it didn’t live up to expectations. The one positive is its location—it’s close to Central Station, making it easy to get around. However, for a more comfortable stay, I’d recommend looking elsewhere.

positive_text: J'imagine que pour des personnes en working holiday c'est un bon moyen d'économiser de l'argent. Mais en tant que voyageurs il y a des hostels beaucoup mieux pour le même prix ou moins cher.
negative_text:
Pas de réception sur place, tout se fait par WhatsApp et les seules personnes qui travaillent sont celles qui viennent pour nettoyer mais elles sont en général pas au courant de chose lier au fonctionnement de l'hôtel.
Donc si vous chercher des bons conseils pour visiter Sydney c'est clairement pas ici que vous les aurez.

Avant même d'arriver j'ai senti le genre d'hôstel: après avoir lu de nombreux commentaires négatifs, j'ai souhaité annuler ma réservation. Comme cela n'est pas proposé dans leurs options quand on réserve, booking a fait une demande à l'hôstel, leur laissant donc le choix d'accéder à ma demande, mais ils ont refusé me disant que c'était le fonctionnement de booking (alors que booking leur laisser le choix). En gros ce qui compte c'est leur argent, pas la satisfaction client.

Ensuite, le jour de mon arrivée, je n'ai pas pu manger le soir car je n'avais pas réservé pour le repas, sachant que la réservation doit se faire avant 16h, que l'on découvre ça une fois que l'on a fait le check in, donc pour ceux qui font un check in après 16h ne comptez pas sur un repas le premier soir.

Les petits déjeuners sont basiques: pain blanc, peanut butter, confiture et café soluble.

Les espaces communs ne sont pas très agréables et donc pas propices pour rencontrer du monde. La terrasse qui avait l'air très chouette sur les photos est en pente et donne sur une palissade en bois (donc oublié la jolie vue derrière). Et vous y rencontrerez de nombreux cafards.

Les lits sont corrects mais il n'y a pas de quoi ouvrir les fenêtres et il fait donc très chaud dans les chambres. Et les clims sont supers bruyantes. Donc au choix: on meurt de chaud où on dort dans le bruit.

Au passage, le dortoir 6 places pour femme dans lequel j'étais est en sous sol avec une grande fenêtre donnant sur la rue, sans rideau, d'où n'importe qui peut donc nous voir.

Foi o hostel mais fraco onde fiquei: mas mais uma vez provavelmente tem um preço justo para o que oferece. Mas comparando com outros da Australia, está abaixo do que mostra nas imagens. Não tem ninguém na receção. Falamos por mensagem e alguém nos entrega as coisas. Demoraram duas semanas a devolver o dinheiro da caução da toalha e secador de cabelo.

title: Crowded, weird vibe
positive_text: Only positives were that the bed had blackout curtains, and there were lockers. The company was pretty responsive on the chat function.
negative_text:
I’m not really sure how this place gets an It was crowded, not nearly enough social areas or showers/toilets for the amount of people staying there. There were clearly quite a few people staying in the hostel longer term and there were peoples personal belongings all over the room, so it felt messy. There were extension cables daisy chained across the room to provide power to the beds which is a massive fire hazard. I counted 6 extensions connected to one wall outlet (it’s an old building so there is clearly a shortage of sockets)
The beds were really creaky so you couldn’t move without disturbing others. Pillows need replacing as well as they were very lumpy.
Breakfast was ok, basic (toast and cereal, instant coffee/tea) also finishes at 9 which is quite early. The free dinner was again basic but tasted pretty good (chicken and rice). The table area is so small though that people were sat in the corridor to eat because there was no space.
Views of the bridge are good from the female bathroom and maybe one or two of the rooms, the fences are too high in the outdoor area to actually see it though.
Biggest annoyance was that there were no staff at the hostel itself, so when you checked in you had to download an app just to be able to get into your room. The doors seem to just be always open and people wander in and out. I had to help a group of older folks check in because they couldn’t work the passcode for the door and there was nobody else to help them.
There are cleaners around sometimes but I don’t think they are directly employed by the property. They also start hoovering at 8am which can be heard all over the building so good luck if you want a lie in.
As I’m backpacking I was looking for a budget option as the options are limited and everywhere is so expensive, but it’s worth paying just a little bit more for much better hostels in Sydney.

Look, a hostel is a hostel: between the bunk beds and the shared bathrooms it’s never going to be an ideal place to stay. However, I felt bamboozled by the other reviews I read, and I just wanted to share my experience so you know what to expect:

For the most part it was cleanly, but I did see a cockroach in the bathroom one day and several cockroaches right outside the building.

The layout of the entire space was strange, I think we had to go on the fire escape to get to our room? And there was another room that you entered from the outside. Our door didn’t always close so I’d sometimes return to an open and unlocked door. That wasn’t a big deal but didn’t feel great in terms of security.

There weren’t very many common spaces - the only common space was the dining room which wasn’t very big. Between this and the small rooms and the no talking rule in rooms, it made it hard to spend time in the hostel. As a result there were often people sitting in stairwells, which sometimes was inconvenient to walk around.

there isn’t any elevator in the space, so when I arrived and left I had to carry my bags up several flights of thin stairs

There were lots or rules and fines. Every day I would get a message about a new rule in the hostel and and the fine we would receive if we violated it. For example, we weren’t allowed to hang towels on bars of beds, but we also weren’t provided hooks to hang towels elsewhere. There seemed to be a lot of surveillance, but I also never saw anyone at the front desk, including both when I checked in and when I checked out.

When you first arrive you have to upload a picture of your passport or else you get locked out. I did that and it was working fine, and then a few hours later it randomly locked me out. I was able to text their off-hours number and they let me back in (their texting service was very responsive), but getting locked out of the place I’m staying for no reason is still a problem.
hotel_response:
Thank you for sharing your detailed feedback. We appreciate your honest review as it helps us improve the guest experience.

To clarify, our hostel operates as a self-check-in setup, which allows guests to access their rooms conveniently. While we don’t have an on-site front desk at all times, our reception team is available 24/7 through remote support to assist with any concerns, as you experienced with the quick response to your lockout issue.

Regarding the no-talking rule in rooms, this is in place to ensure a restful environment for all guests, as shared spaces require mutual respect for each other's resting hours. We understand this can feel restrictive but strive to balance comfort and convenience for everyone staying with us.

Your other points about space, cleanliness, and layout have been noted, and we are actively working to address areas where we can improve.

As far as I am aware nothing was said to this guest and he blamed me for his own mixup.

I came back to my room one day with everything in the previously mentioned storage/sink area thrown on the floor in a pile. The next day the staff came in the room to tell us to tidy the room??? The mess was made by the staff with no explanation. His response? “I’m one of the good guys” then proceeds to take photos of our belongings.

Food service/cleaners look overworked and mentioned several times their pay is very low (I actually think below minimum wage).

Unusually, no staff living onsite so at night any issue takes over an hour for someone to travel to the site to resolve (e.g. loud noises from the terrace area at 1am).

title: Brilliant value, would stay again!
positive_text:
Easy to get to, simple check-in, felt pretty secure and I appreciated the no talking in rooms rule. Encourages people to sit out in the main area - though the main area is quite small from what I saw. Great blockout curtains, and I had a little aircon remote next to my bed. I forgot to use it, but nice to have.

Awesome that for the price you can also get dinner included - I wish I'd downloaded the check in app sooner; I didn't realise you'd need to register to be included (but makes sense!). The app was a surprise, too, but I found I liked using it. Staff were very quick & responsive when I had a question.

Having an ensuite connected to the room is awesome - it's a tiny bathroom, but it was nice and reduces the chance of waiting. There were several other bathrooms nearby if needed, so no issue there.

Found the bed quite comfy! The pillow was great, the mattress quite firm - in a good way. I usually like a softer mattress, but it wasn't a problem at all.

Great location too - very easy to get to and from the airport and walk to other areas; also easy walking distance (under 20 mins) to heaps of art galleries.
negative_text:
I found it strange how high up the ladders/steps were for the bunk beds. I'm usually all about climbing and top bunking, but found it quite awkward to climb up and down. That was it really! I was only there for one night, so had very little exposure to anything else.

Not really a dislike, but worth knowing: you can't store your belongings onsite for more than 2 hours after checkout, but that's because they have tight security protocol. Not something I'd ask to change. You're already getting a pretty great deal anyway - so it would have just topped it off if that was possible.

Oh, and I was very nervous about my phone battery dying and not being able to get into the hostel/my room if something happened to my phone, but it just meant I committed the backup code to memory all the more. I didn't see if there was a solution to this, but there would be one available I'm sure.

positive_text:
Struttura abbastanza centrale, molto vicino alla zona di Darling Harbour e Barangaroo.
Camera e bagno in camera abbastanza puliti: bagno con doccia ampia.
Presenza di altri bagni e doccie al di fuori della camera (in condivisione con gli altri ospiti dell'ostello).
Armadietto di piccole dimensioni per ogni ospite della stanza (senza lucchetto). Spazio sotto i letti a castello per riporre le valigie.
Ogni letto è fornito di due prese elettriche che però non sempre funzionano.
Presenza di un condizionatore per scaldare e raffreddare la stanza.
Si accede alla struttura (entrata, camera, ecc.) uilizzando l'app Goki che permette di aprere le porte usando il proprio telefono senza avere chiavi. Facile e rapido anche il processo di check-in sempre attraverso la stessa applicazione.
negative_text:
Struttura non facilmente raggiungibile con i mezzi.
Stanza femminile da 14 persone molto piccola: difficile muoversi e aprire le valigie se tutti gli ospiti sono presenti.
Una finestra dietro ad un letto a castello che non viene aperta: la stanza sa da chiuso.
Un unico bagno in camera per 14 persone non è sufficiente.
No ascensore: difficile raggiungere il secondo piano avendo valigie molto grandi e pesanti.
Deposito bagagli post check-out disponibile solo dalle 10 alle 12 della mattina.
La struttura offre colazione e cena: nonostante sia piacevole, la scelta è veramente limitata e il menù propone sempre le stesse cose. Ogni ospite lava i propri piatti dopo colazione e cena.

title: Very clean hostel but not a lot of room, but close to everything. Overall a convenient place
positive_text: I stayed at the hostel in a 6 women bunk room for a month and half in the winter. Their provided meals for breakfast and dinner where always good and the people serving were always so nice. I really enjoyed the cleanliness of the hostel. It was always for the most part taken very well care of. I liked the kitchen supplies were supplied, including tea kettles and a toaster. If there were large issues maintenance cleared it up very quickly and they were always responsive, reachable, and helpful through the WhatsApp. The water was always hot. And wifi was very fast and easy to use and the blackout curtains on each bunk was so nice and created excellent privacy. The location was very very convenient. Across the street from Central Station and the major bus stop. Also close to the bars and nightlife so it was easy to just walk over. Very close to convenience stores and 7min walk to large shopping malls and grocery stores like, Coles. It was directly located on top of a Thai restaurant which was just kind of cool to tell people. I never tried it but smelled good. And you could never smell it or hear the noise from inside.
negative_text: Sometimes the staff had an attitude which made you feel uncomfortable at times, my one experience with that was in the morning. There's no common room just a kitchen and dining room with only 6 chairs, which led a lot of people having to eat their food standing around the room. It is a lot smaller than the photos led you on to believe it is. There is not a lot of room for people to store groceries and no freezer or oven. I traveled during the winter for a month and stayed in a 6 women bunk room on the top floor and there was no source of heat so you were freezing each night. There's no reception and you just have to message them on the WhatsApp, which was fine with me but a lot of older residents had a lot of trouble. There's no signs so the building is hard to find and there's no instructions on how to check out. Very small hostel so it felt very cramped at times and didn't have places for people to sit because there wasn't a common room. People could only talk in the kitchen or in the stairwells which made it cramped as well. If you are staying on the top bunk they are almost impossible to get into. Very hard to get up the ladder and dangerous at times. Right next to a tobacco shop which was fine, but there was always a homeless woman outside of it that would yell at people walking by.

positive_text: I liked how we were able to get as much breakfast as we could. I liked the general vibe of the visitors, friendly and considerate. I also appreciate how I was able to get a room change after realising my original room was deafening from the busy road right outside my window.

I didn't like how there was: no on-site reception, no buffet option for the dinners, rude behaviour from the head chef and how the cleaning staff had poor hygiene habits (casually dropped washed bedsheets and washed blankets on the FLOOR before setting them up on beds). There were many visitors who wanted to eat more than one serving of the complimentary dinners, but the head chef refused to give them a second serving until after everyone else had eaten a first serving. I think free dinners should have a buffet-style system where everyone gets their own serving. It's extremely inefficient to have everyone line up with only one person serving. To solve these issues, I think it should be on a first come first serve basis, or the free dinner duration should be longer. I personally wasn't able to eat the dinners most evenings because my circumstances didn't allow me to arrive at the hostel before 18:30. A "free" dinner shouldn't be called free if it's only available from 17:45-18:30, as most travellers expect dinner time to be between 6-8pm. I was appalled by the greediness and inconsiderate nature of the timing, and of the quality of food. When I arrived on my first evening, we were served pasta without any meat whatsoever, that came with a sour pungent smell. It was shockingly unappetizing.

5 bathrooms out of 15 bathrooms were permanently sealed off for unstated reasons, severely limiting showering capacity and inconveniencing visitors by making us queue up. All in all, it appears that management don't really care about the wellbeing of its visitors.

negative_text:
Some tips to future travelers.

1). I would say there is no reception in this property so you need to manage your payment online. Make sure you have enough fund in the bank card and the card can do online transactions on the day you check in.

2). You can send the photo id to mailto:reception@venushostels.com.au. In this way they will do the check in for you so no need to download the app.

I felt like a criminal with someone there waiting for me to leave.

I had no idea who the staff team was during my entire time, so there wasn’t anyone to discuss things with. I don’t think they have anyone managing at the property tbh. Most people I spoke had no clue- it was the blind leading the blind

I wasn’t able to relax and just felt like I was always being watched and reported.

Rules of the house are over emphasised with messages and posters all of the place. Rules which I respect, but it was just too much.

A poster in the room stating if you were caught on your phone in the room you’ll be removed of the premises 😂🙈. Extreme.

title: Met all my needs with some minor problems
positive_text:
Although it’s scary not having any staff in person to communicate with when problems arise, the staff responded promptly when you messaged them online.
My stay was comfortable and if you’re like me in that when you travel you don’t care too much about where you stay because you’re out most of the day and just need somewhere to shower and sleep then this place is perfect. The bed is comfy - just be aware that the blanket they provide is not sufficient for winter. The other girls staying there were nice and respectful and I felt secure leaving my luggage at the place every day. It’s also in such a convenient location which I feel is one of the best parts about staying here. You’re close to all the main attractions in Sydney and I enjoyed being in walking distance to everywhere I wanted to visit. It felt safe walking back here at night.
negative_text:
The cleanliness of the place was just not bad. I wouldn’t say the place is clean. For me, the cleanliness of the bed and bathrooms were the most important. The bed was clean, but the bathrooms were visibly a bit grimy. Two of the bathrooms are inconveniently arranged; the toilet, sink and shower are strangely positioned and don’t have places to hang your towel or put your toiletries while you shower. The third bathroom is well arranged and has ample space though. The water temperature is really hard to adjust though. My shower took so much longer because every few minutes the water would just go cold and you had to wait a few minutes for it to warm up again.
Sleeping might be difficult for light sleepers since you’re next to a main road and it’s constantly really noisy even through the night. For me it wasn’t too much of a problem and I feel like it’s a sacrifice you make to be close to the city.
A small problem I had was not having blinds for my bed. I didn’t mind because I wasn’t doing much in my bed other than sleeping and the other girls in my room respected my privacy but it would have been nice to have them for the extra privacy. Another small problem was not being aware I needed a lock to use the in-room lockers before arriving. It was a minor problem but it would have been nice to not take time out to buy a new lock when I could’ve brought one from home if I knew.

positive_text: The beds mattress was nice, the dhna was lovely and soft the privacy curtains were great and velvet same as the duna absolutely fantastic. The ensuite bathroom was convenient. I really loved the breakfast and dinner that was provided. That especially made it stand out from venus' other hostels. Especially their Potts point hostel in comparison to this one potts point was not great. But this hostel got most things right. The price was great, the quiet policies were upheld, the bathroom worked well and wasn't missing bits. The bedding was lovely, the curtains were fantastic and the doona oh my god that doona was soft and lovely. Dinner was wonderful I made friends there. Breakfast was quiet. The lockers were nice although they are missing an opportunity by not adding lockable drawers like taquila sunrise hostel has under the beds that would increase luggage storage space. They have lots of food pantry storage for each room. The set up is pretty good. They had wifi which was good. They have luggage storage which was fantastic and they even sent me a list of places to go and things tonsee and do in the area which was fantastic with great detail on it. The hostel was quiet and I was able to sleep during the day and night. The other guests were respectful and friendly.
negative_text:
There should be a handle on the top or side of the top bunk because its difficult getting in and out of it.
They should send you check-in information the day before not the day of your booking and only just before you're supposed to arrive. The goki app is great and worked just fine for me but having that information the day before would have significantly reduced my stress and made the process smoother and more efficient.
Check-in earlier would have been really good rather than waiting outside for 3 hours. The signage on the outside of the hostel could be improved as it wasnt obvious or easy to find the hostel or the front door.

When I asked what would be done to make it up to me, they told me "we will reimburse the difference of price. 35$ overall" I said that this was the logical thing to do (even if that price difference was ridiculous - again, 35$ over 6nights!!!), but that it wasn't what I meant, because I was expecting a goodwill gesture for 1) the inconvenience of having to stay in a bigger room 2) the stress and the time it added to my trip. The person replied that nothing could be done and that if I wasn't happy, again, I "had the choice" to cancel. After long negotiations where I asked to talk to the management (I could sense the employee was under pressure and could do nothing even if she wanted to - don't blame her), she told me she would try to get back to me with a real peace offering. Later that day, I received a... 10$ voucher to spend on another stay in one of their properties. What a joke. I've contacted Booking but nothing has been resolved yet. This is what happens when businesses decide to do everything from a remote office - No-one feels accountable and guests are left feeling like mere financial transactions rather than valued individuals.

title: Inexpensive but sketchy and extremely run down. I regret staying here.
positive_text: It was cheap. The location isn't exactly central, but you can reach Darling Harbor pretty easily, and you can also get to Chinatown and the Rocks/Circular Quay if you're willing to walk around 20 minutes. Also, the staff were extremely responsive and helpful on WhatsApp. They seem like lovely people, which raised my expectations before arriving.
negative_text: However, cleanliness was a huge issue. I can't say much of the rooms (since I arrived late at night and left early the next morning, so it was dark). But as for the shower, even if you adjust your standards to hostels (which people don't particularly stay at for comfort reasons) it was completely unacceptable. The shower head was completely broken and hanging off the wall and barely released any water, and the surrounding floor and wall tiles were cracked and slightly moldy. The floor was also visibly dirty, and the shower I used near my room had a small window that couldn't be closed, which (if you're tall enough) makes you visible from any floor of the central "atrium" area of the building. I sincerely hope that I just got the one bad shower room, which would explain why all the other ones were occupied when I checked. Also, the one staff member that was there and brought me to my room also briefly ruffled through one of the clearly occupied bunk beds, which made me quite uncomfortable. I also didn't feel safe walking through the neighborhood on the way there (albeit it was past 9 PM). I think this place has potential to be a good cheap place to stay, but currently it's way too sketchy and run down, even though it's cheap. There are other equally cheap hostels in better locations that are also much higher quality, so look elsewhere.

여행객이고, 잠만 자고 나오기에 좋은 숙소입니다. 거실이 넓지 않아 개인적인 업무를 하기엔 어려움이 있지만, 잠을 자고, 샤워하고, 식사를 하기에 무리가 없는 숙소입니다. 숙박비를 아끼고 싶은 여행객에게 좋은 숙소에요. 추천드립니다.
